question: Card eight of the vision on jaws-v1: Irencrag Pyromancer (0/4 Human; 3 damage to any target whenever you draw your second card each turn, on any player's turn) back in -- the pilot: 'I love that' -- and for what?

contributions.text:
Irencrag Pyromancer (014). Pick: in for Voracious Greatshark (contested).
- History: in from v0.1.0 to v1.3.0; left at v2.0.0 (voltron-v1 merge, 2026-10-24) with the whole draw/ping package (Niv-Mizzet, Psychosis Crawler, Razorkin Needlehead, Fevered Visions, Faerie Mastermind, Library of Leng, Shark Typhoon). No reason for this card alone in branch.json, decisions.jsonl, the log or CONTEXT — swept out by the equipment-voltron frame. That reason no longer holds: shabraz-v1 and jaws-v1 brought back Mastermind, Leng, Typhoon, Magus, Time Reversal and Big Score; the deck is draw-first again.
- Fit: removal and reach, not draw. It kills an X/3 such as Krenko (game 008). The audit has interaction-breadth UNDER (3 classes vs 5) and sweepers UNDER (0). Ageless Insight and Bard turn a non-draw-step draw into two; Sphinx alone fires it on every opponent's turn.
- Cost of cutting Greatshark: the only counter to a creature or artifact spell (staged 2026-11-14 for exactly that); Pyromancer answers the creature after it lands. The pilot OKs Shark cuts. A 5-drop for a 3-drop permanent (MV<=3 creatures 12 to 13).
- Goldfish, one instrument (reads only the face damage, not the removal): 3 better, 4 worse, 10 no call; damage @T10 -3.2 [-4.2, -2.1]; board power @T6 -0.2.
- Second pick: Mountain (37 to 36), not recommended: red 1 short, missed drop by T5 +2.7 pts [+2.3, +3.1], mulligans +1.4 pts [+1.2, +1.7] — feeds the slowness.

contributions.slice: MODE prescribe re-run with wheels open; verbatim
contributions.text:
Re-run with every rule lifted and wheels open: the same two swaps.
- Wheel screen, Winds of Change as the cut (goldfish, one instrument): finisher wheel by T8 -6.5 pts [-7.0, -6.0], damage @T10 -9.2 [-11.0, -7.4], wheels cast by T10 -0.38; better on dead wheels in hand (-0.022) and the keep rule (+2.7 pts) — partly backs "too many wheels", far outweighed. The Greatshark cut cost only 3.2 damage [-4.2, -2.1], no call on the finisher wheel.
- Pyromancer: on a competitive bracket-3 table a 3-mana repeatable answer that kills X/3s is worth more than a 5-mana counter that only stops creature and artifact spells.
- Theorist: Shark Typhoon is a 6-mana enchantment almost always cycled, in practice a spell; Theorist puts a 2-drop Human permanent in its place. Painful: an instant-speed draw that leaves a flying Shark, and stack 012 orphaned.
- If a wheel goes anyway: Time Reversal, not Winds — it shuffles (Theorist can never recur it), wipes the graveyard Theorist feeds from, costs 5. Judgment only, unmeasured; any wheel cut costs real finisher rate.
- Lizard Blades stays second choice for Theorist's slot; Unsettled Mariner stays.

call.pilot_words: a counter target spell on a 5 CMC 5/5 body... it's bad... the only reason it's in is because it's a shark
call.reading: Irencrag Pyromancer back in for Voracious Greatshark: a cheap repeatable answer and reach off the deck's draws, for an expensive Shark the pilot judged was in for its type.
